title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution underscores the importance of safeguarding religious freedom while urging that artificial intelligence systems be guided by authoritative texts and operated with clear transparency. It calls for robust oversight and transparent policies to ensure AI tools respect diverse beliefs and avoid bias.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress on how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under the 702 provisions of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report will assess the impact, safeguards, and implications of AI in foreign intelligence activities and data handling.

title: To authorize certain labor market data collection activities and to improve Federal measurement of the workforce impacts of artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy authorizes the collection of labor market data so the federal government can better understand how artificial intelligence affects jobs and the overall workforce. It also aims to improve federal measurement and tracking of AI’s impacts on employment and related labor market outcomes.

title: To require entities to include human-controlled shutdown mechanisms in all artificial intelligence systems.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: This policy mandates that all artificial intelligence systems must be equipped with a human‑controlled shutdown feature. The goal is to ensure that people can immediately stop an AI from operating if it behaves unexpectedly or poses a risk.

title: To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to carry out prize competitions to advance the science of interpretability and to develop adversarial robustness with respect to artificial intelligence products, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to organize prize competitions that advance the science of AI interpretability and strengthen adversarial robustness of AI products. It also includes additional measures related to these goals.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to keep consumers safe by making sure AI systems are clear, honest, and not misleading. It sets rules that require AI content to be properly labeled and bans deceptive practices that could trick or harm users.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes setting up a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate incidents and compliance related to cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. It also includes additional provisions to address related regulatory or oversight matters beyond the board’s core responsibilities.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill proposes creating the Artificial Intelligence Horizon Fund to support research, development, and deployment of AI technologies. It also includes provisions for additional, unspecified purposes related to AI policy and oversight.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a new law that sets rules for how AI models are developed, tested, and used, requiring companies to disclose key details about their models. It aims to make AI more transparent, safe, and fair by mandating risk assessments, data‑handling best practices, and accountability for any harms caused.

title: To establish a human-centered Federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce, promote the ethical and responsible teaching and learning of artificial intelligence, provide for equitable access to artificial intelligence-ready workforce development, safeguard student and worker data privacy, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy aims to create a federal framework that puts people at the center of using AI in schools and jobs. It focuses on teaching AI responsibly, ensuring fair access to AI training, protecting the privacy of students and workers, and covering other related goals.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act seeks to shield households from rising energy bills caused by the expanding use of AI data centers. It would require data centers to meet stricter energy‑efficiency standards and provide rebates or subsidies to help keep home electricity costs affordable.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act establishes a new federal agency dedicated to advancing AI research, development, and innovation. It outlines the department’s role in promoting responsible AI use, setting safety standards, and coordinating policy and investment across industry and academia.

title: A bill to establish the Department of Artificial Intelligence and to provide for the regulation of advanced artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new government Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee AI research and development. It also introduces regulations to govern the use of advanced AI systems and includes additional related provisions.

title: A bill to require disclosure of certain information relating to artificial intelligence systems, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill would mandate that companies disclose specific details about their AI systems, such as how they were trained, what data they use, and how they make decisions. The aim is to increase transparency and accountability in AI development and deployment, with additional provisions for related regulatory purposes.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to regulate the use of artificial intelligence tools within the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. It seeks to ensure that AI systems used for veteran care are safe, transparent, and respectful of veterans’ privacy and rights.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act seeks to regulate the creation and deployment of artificial intelligence systems that might pose risks to society. It proposes strict oversight, transparency, and penalties to prevent the use of AI technologies that could act unpredictably or harmfully.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act establishes clear rules for how artificial intelligence can be used in processing Veterans Affairs claims, ensuring transparency, fairness, and safeguards against bias. It sets out requirements for auditing, documentation, and oversight of AI systems to protect veterans’ rights and improve the integrity of claim decisions.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a law that bans the deployment of certain AI technologies within specified covered sectors. It establishes restrictions to protect safety, privacy, and national security by limiting the use of these AI systems.

title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act sets rules for making sure AI systems used by the military are reliable, safe, and work as intended. It requires regular reports and oversight to keep the government and the public informed about how those AI systems are performing.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how and why it uses artificial intelligence in its services. The law aims to increase accountability and protect veterans by ensuring AI systems are transparent, fair, and aligned with patients’ best interests.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a pilot program that uses AI to defend critical infrastructure against cyber threats. It also outlines related responsibilities and objectives for ensuring the program’s effectiveness and coordination with other agencies.

title: Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act seeks to prohibit Medicare from refusing coverage for AI‑driven medical services. It ensures that AI‑assisted care is fully reimbursable, protecting beneficiaries from coverage denials.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act would temporarily halt the construction or expansion of new data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. It aims to curb the rapid growth of AI infrastructure and address concerns over energy use, environmental impact, and regulatory oversight.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act is designed to stop companies from inflating AI service prices and fixing wages for workers in the AI industry. It proposes rules and penalties that would enforce fair pricing and equitable pay for AI-related work.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a law designed to protect AI developers by making it illegal to steal, copy, or redistribute their models without permission. It imposes penalties for those who violate these protections and provides enforcement mechanisms to help creators secure their intellectual property.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 creates a framework to guide the use and study of artificial intelligence within the judicial system. It establishes independent bodies to monitor AI applications, ensure fairness and transparency, and protect privacy while encouraging research to improve court efficiency.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 outlines how the Small Business Administration will use AI technologies to improve its services and decision‑making. It establishes guidelines, oversight, and safeguards to ensure responsible, transparent, and equitable AI deployment in government operations.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act proposes federal measures to position the United States as a global leader in AI technology. It aims to create a unified regulatory framework that ensures consistent standards, safety, and ethical practices across all AI developments nationwide.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 establishes a national framework to assess, monitor, and mitigate risks associated with the deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It requires companies and agencies to conduct risk analyses, report findings, and implement safeguards to protect public safety, privacy, and economic stability.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act promotes the integration and development of artificial intelligence technologies within the financial sector, aiming to enhance efficiency, customer experience, and innovation. It sets guidelines for responsible AI use, establishes regulatory frameworks, and encourages collaboration between financial institutions and technology providers to ensure safe and compliant deployment of AI solutions.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act is a proposed law designed to strengthen artificial intelligence research capabilities at Historically Black Colleges and Universities. It seeks to provide funding, infrastructure, and collaborative opportunities to help these institutions become leading centers for AI innovation and education.
